chunks: And in the narration of al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, he said:

He was asked, while I was present, about a man who performed eight circuits around the House. So he said, "Voluntary or obligatory?" He said, "Obligatory." He said, "He should add six to it, and when he finishes, he should pray two rak'ahs at the Maqam of Ibrahim عليه السلام, then go out to al-Safa and al-Marwah and perform tawaf between them. Then when he finishes, he should pray another two rak'ahs, so it will be a voluntary tawaf and an obligatory tawaf."

key_terms.بِٱلْبَيْتِ: around the Ka'bah, the Sacred House
key_terms.مَقَامِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ: the Station of Ibrahim عليه السلام where tawaf prayer is performed
key_terms.نَافِلَةً: a supererogatory or voluntary act of worship
key_terms.ٱلصَّفَا وَٱلْمَرْوَةِ: the two sacred points between which sa'i is performed

ai.seo_question: What should someone do if he performs eight circuits in an obligatory tawaf?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling for one who performs eight circuits in an obligatory tawaf by mistake. The Imam عليه السلام instructs him to add six more circuits so that the total becomes two complete tawafs, one counted as obligatory and the other as supererogatory, with the related prayers and sa'i performed accordingly.
